title: Golden Axe Warrior
subtitle: Death Adder’s world to explore
summary: Golden Axe Warrior is Sega's overhead action adventure, first released for Master System in North America in April 1991.
body: Golden Axe Warrior is Sega's overhead action adventure, first released for Master System in North America in April 1991. A young warrior crosses Firewood and its neighbouring lands to recover nine crystals and confront Death Adder. The familiar enemy connects it to Golden Axe, while towns, hidden labyrinths and an explorable overworld give the journey a different structure. Direct fighting takes place inside those spaces, with collected equipment and learned magic steadily expanding the hero's options. Reaching the tyrant depends on finding what his conquest has scattered across the world.

Each crystal is held in a labyrinth containing enemies, puzzles and a guarding boss. Locating those places is part of the task, with more than two hundred overworld screens providing a landscape to search. Towns offer equipment and supplies bought with horns gathered from enemies. Improved weapons and armour strengthen the warrior, while magical abilities consume a limited stock of pots. The journey therefore moves between discovery and preparation, as the next hidden passage may ask for an item or enough resources to survive the dungeon beyond it.

An axe can cut down trees, while Earth magic clears rocks, allowing ordinary scenery to conceal another route. Acquiring those tools changes what the player can investigate in places already visited. Gathering the nine crystals eventually opens the final labyrinth, where the Golden Axe itself becomes essential to confronting Death Adder. Chikako Kamatani composed the music. The adventure's appeal lies in the changing relationship with its map: a screen that once seemed closed can reveal another purpose after the warrior returns with the ability to alter it.
